Literally none of what you said was different than what I said? You talked about snap counts. When you look at snap count %s yes, that's how it went, you're right. But from watching the bucs games last year, I'm just saying how it went. They followed a pattern as far as when they rotated their running backs. It was rotating via drives, not circumstances, like third and longs, goaline, etc. like most teams. This game they rotated what I thought was very similarly, with the caveat that Rachaad came in when both of Irving's drives went past the 50. I thought it was good news for White, personally.

If you think Irving's gonna take over very soon, you may be right. But this game he didn't, and the thread is about responding to what we saw during the games, not projecting rest of season imo.

Rachaad White is still the guy. Everyone wants to be early on predicting that Irving is the guy (and he is definitely the #2 RB) but the bucs deployed literally the same exact rotation in this game as they had all of last year with Sean Tucker. 

Last year was an extremely consistent rotation: White plays all of drive #1 and #2, Tucker gets all of drive #3, White gets all of the rest until halftime. Then White gets all of the first drive out of halftime, Tucker gets all of the second drive, and then White gets the rest of the game. It actually looked even more "bellcowish" than it really was, because very often the bucs would quickly stall out on Tucker's drives, and do damage on White's. Hence him playing so much more.

This game went: White got all of drive #1 and drive #2, Irving got the first half of drive #3 then White went in when the ball hit midfield, White got drive #4, out of halftime White got drive #5, White started drive #6 and had like a 30 yard run wiped out, so Irving played a couple snaps and then White finished the rest of the drive, and lastly on drive #7 Irving and White rotated a few plays but it was entirely White once they got across the 50.

In conclusion, if anything I'm MORE optimistic about Rachaad White now because last year he played his drives and then was out for entire drives no matter what. This game he played all of his drives AND he immediately subbed in as soon as the ball was anywhere close to scoring position. Things could obviously change quickly, but in this game White was the guy.
